articles.title: We all share a 15-acre Georgian mansion for the price of a two-bed house
articles.summary: Co-housing residents live in a Grade II listed mansion for the same price as a two-bed house.
articles.content:
Residents range in age from seven to 70. This summer, however, the balance will shift towards a younger demographic, as two older residents are leaving and two families with three children aged from six to 12 will be moving in.

There is a four-stage application process to become a community member.

"We know that the more effort we put into the application process, the better chance it's going to work and it's going to be a good fit," says Louise.

Jenny Kincova, 64, the longest current resident of nine years' standing, is one of those moving on to live in Llanidloes itself, like a number of previous residents.

She says of her move to Dol-llys: "I was on my own. My girls had left home. I didn't just want to move to a place and not know anyone. Once I moved here, I was really excited by the prospect of communal decision-making and cooperative community living."

Although she still enjoys the communal living, she has started to find the "emotional energy" needed for decision-making and keeping a group together tiring.

"I don't want to lose contact with here at all," she said.

"As you can see, we still get on, it's not about that at all. It's just about change again.

"I'm not going to have all this space and I'm not going to live in a listed building."

The hall offers free allotments to locals in exchange for some help on their work days, holds open days, lets groups use its communal rooms for things like yoga classes, and will be holding its first board games weekend this summer.

Its residents even gave the hall to friends for free to use as their wedding venue.

It has recently hosted volunteer workers from the Wwoof (Worldwide Opportunities on Organic Farms) organisation, where people get free board and lodging for two weeks while helping out with projects in the grounds and learning skills.
articles.reasoning: The article describes a successful co-housing community living affordably in a large historic mansion, fostering intergenerational communal living, cooperative decision-making, and community engagement through shared spaces and volunteer programs. This represents a positive social innovation with meaningful impact on quality of life and community building for a diverse group of residents and the local area.
articles.personality_title: Families share life in a historic mansion for the price of a small house
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In a quiet area, a large old mansion known as a Grade II listed building is home to a mix of people from children to seniors. Instead of living alone, they share this big house together as a community.

**What happened** – This summer, the community will change as two older residents move out and two families with young children move in. To join, new members go through a careful four-step application to make sure they fit well with the group. One long-time resident, Jenny, is leaving after nine years because she finds the group decisions tiring, but she still values the friendships and the communal lifestyle.

**Impact** – Living together this way lets people afford a large, beautiful home for the same price as a small two-bedroom house. The community shares not only the living space but also work and events, like gardening, yoga classes, and even hosting weddings. They welcome volunteers who help with the grounds and learn new skills, creating a lively, supportive environment for all ages.

**What's next step** – As new families join, the community will keep growing and changing. They plan to hold more events, like a board games weekend, to bring everyone closer. The group will continue to balance sharing responsibilities and making decisions together, while offering space and activities for both residents and local people.

**One-sentence takeaway** – A group of families and individuals live affordably and happily together in a historic mansion by sharing space, work, and community life.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des familles partagent une vie dans un manoir historique au prix d’une petite maison
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Dans une région calme, un grand ancien manoir classé Grade II abrite un groupe de personnes allant des enfants aux seniors. Au lieu de vivre seuls, ils partagent cette grande maison ensemble en communauté.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Cet été, la communauté va changer : deux résidents âgés partent et deux familles avec de jeunes enfants arrivent. Pour rejoindre, les nouveaux membres passent par une candidature en quatre étapes pour bien s’intégrer au groupe. Une résidente de longue date, Jenny, quitte après neuf ans car les décisions de groupe sont fatigantes, mais elle apprécie toujours les amitiés et le mode de vie commun.

**Impact** – Vivre ainsi ensemble permet d’habiter une grande et belle maison pour le même prix qu’un petit appartement de deux chambres. La communauté partage non seulement l’espace de vie mais aussi le travail et des événements, comme le jardinage, des cours de yoga, et même des mariages. Ils accueillent des bénévoles qui aident dans les jardins et apprennent de nouvelles compétences, créant un environnement vivant et solidaire pour tous les âges.

**Prochaine étape** – À mesure que de nouvelles familles arrivent, la communauté continue de grandir et d’évoluer. Ils prévoient d’organiser plus d’événements, comme un week-end de jeux de société, pour renforcer les liens. Le groupe continuera à partager les responsabilités et à prendre des décisions ensemble, tout en offrant des espaces et des activités aux résidents et aux habitants locaux.

**En une phrase** – Un groupe de familles et d’individus vivent ensemble à prix abordable et heureux dans un manoir historique en partageant espace, travail et vie communautaire.
articles.personality_title_es: Familias comparten vida en una mansión histórica por el precio de una casa pequeña
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En una zona tranquila, una gran mansión antigua, catalogada como Grade II, es hogar de personas de todas las edades, desde niños hasta personas mayores. En lugar de vivir solos, comparten esta gran casa como una comunidad.

**Qué pasó** – Este verano, la comunidad cambiará: dos residentes mayores se mudan y dos familias con niños pequeños llegan. Para unirse, los nuevos miembros pasan por un proceso de solicitud de cuatro etapas para asegurar que encajen bien en el grupo. Una residente de larga duración, Jenny, se va después de nueve años porque las decisiones en grupo le resultan cansadoras, pero valora las amistades y el estilo de vida comunal.

**Impacto** – Vivir juntos así permite a las personas pagar por una casa grande y hermosa el mismo precio que una casa pequeña de dos habitaciones. La comunidad comparte no solo el espacio, sino también el trabajo y eventos como jardinería, clases de yoga e incluso bodas. Reciben voluntarios que ayudan en el terreno y aprenden nuevas habilidades, creando un ambiente animado y solidario para todas las edades.

**Próximo paso** – A medida que nuevas familias se unan, la comunidad seguirá creciendo y cambiando. Planean organizar más eventos, como un fin de semana de juegos de mesa, para fortalecer los lazos. El grupo continuará compartiendo responsabilidades y tomando decisiones juntos, mientras ofrece espacios y actividades para residentes y locales.

**Una frase para llevar** – Un grupo de familias e individuos vive de forma asequible y feliz en una mansión histórica, compartiendo espacio, trabajo y vida comunitaria.
